title: Mechanisms of Acquired Resistance to CDK4/6 Inhibition in Hormone Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Adding palbociclib or ribociclib to an aromatase inhibitor or to fulvestrant roughly doubles progression-free survival in hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer, yet nearly every tumor eventually resumes growth. The molecular basis of resistance to CDK4/6 inhibition remains poorly defined because paired pre-treatment and progression tissue is rarely obtained. We have assembled a cohort of 340 patients beginning first-line CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy under a protocol mandating baseline biopsy, plasma collection every 8 weeks, and optional biopsy at progression. Preliminary sequencing of 96 progression specimens identified RB1 truncating events, CCNE1 amplification, FGFR1 gain, and PIK3CA and ESR1 substitutions that were undetectable in the matched pre-treatment sample. This proposal will define the frequency, timing, and functional consequence of these lesions and determine whether their appearance in circulating tumor DNA precedes radiographic progression by a clinically useful interval.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1 will define the spectrum of alterations that appear during CDK4/6 inhibitor exposure by comparing whole-exome and RNA sequencing of 120 matched pre-treatment and progression biopsies, with prespecified attention to RB1 truncating and copy-number events, CCNE1 amplification, FGFR1 gain, and ESR1 ligand-binding domain substitutions. Aim 2 will determine whether these lesions are detectable in serial plasma before imaging changes, applying a 74-gene tumor-informed panel to approximately 2,400 specimens drawn every 8 weeks from 340 participants. Aim 3 will test, in a prospective sub-study of 90 patients, whether plasma detection of RB1 loss identifies those who derive no further disease control from continued CDK4/6 blockade when the endocrine partner is switched, using a co-primary endpoint of progression-free survival and depth of tumor shrinkage.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Endocrine resistance is the dominant clinical problem in hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, accounting for most of the 42,000 annual breast cancer deaths in the United States. CDK4/6 inhibitors delay it but do not prevent it: median progression-free survival in the first-line setting is approximately 24 months, and second-line options remain largely empiric. Small retrospective series report RB1 alterations in roughly 5 percent of progression samples and cyclin E1 pathway activation in a further 15 to 20 percent, but these estimates derive from convenience cohorts without matched baselines, so it is unknown which events are selected under drug pressure and which were present all along. A prospectively collected, uniformly treated cohort with dense circulating tumor DNA sampling is required to separate the two possibilities and to prioritize combinations for testing.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Three features distinguish this proposal. First, biopsy at progression is a protocol requirement rather than an option, and our pilot achieved 71 percent capture, far above the 20 to 30 percent typical of correlative studies. Second, plasma is banked every 8 weeks from treatment start, giving a temporal resolution sufficient to date the appearance of lesions that were absent from the pre-treatment specimen and to estimate the interval between their emergence and imaging change. Third, we couple sequencing to a functional interpretation framework in which each candidate alteration is scored against an eleven-gene E2F transcriptional output signature measured in the same tumor, so that copy-number and transcriptional evidence are integrated rather than reported separately. This design converts a descriptive catalogue into testable, time-resolved hypotheses about how the disease escapes.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Participants receive physician-choice endocrine therapy plus palbociclib or ribociclib on an institutional registry protocol. Baseline and progression cores undergo whole-exome sequencing at 200-fold mean target coverage and RNA sequencing to 40 million paired reads. Plasma undergoes hybrid-capture sequencing at 20,000-fold raw depth with unique molecular identifiers, giving a limit of detection near 0.1 percent variant allele fraction. Variants seen in matched leukocyte DNA are removed before analysis. Timing analyses use a joint model in which plasma variant allele fraction trajectories are fitted as piecewise-linear splines and the change point is compared with the RECIST progression date. With 340 participants and an anticipated 240 progression events we have 84 percent power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.60 associated with acquired RB1 loss at a two-sided alpha of 0.05.

title: ESR1 Mutation Dynamics and Next-Generation Oral Endocrine Agents in Advanced Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Activating mutations in the ligand-binding domain of ESR1 arise under the selective pressure of estrogen deprivation and are found in 20 to 40 percent of patients with aromatase inhibitor-exposed metastatic breast cancer. They render the receptor constitutively active, confer endocrine resistance, and are readily measured in circulating tumor DNA. What remains unclear is how these mutations behave over time on treatment, whether specific substitutions differ in their sensitivity to newer oral antiestrogens, and whether treating on the basis of plasma detection improves outcome. This project will characterize ESR1 mutation kinetics in 500 patients sampled every 4 weeks, compare the pharmacology of Y537S, D538G, E380Q, and L536P receptors against fulvestrant, elacestrant, camizestrant, and imlunestrant, and embed a plasma-directed switching strategy within an investigator-initiated randomized trial, NCT03466099.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1 will quantify the temporal behavior of ESR1 ligand-binding domain mutations during aromatase inhibitor and fulvestrant therapy using droplet digital PCR for eight recurrent substitutions plus targeted sequencing, in 500 patients sampled every 4 weeks for up to 30 months. Aim 2 will define substitution-specific pharmacology by expressing each mutant receptor at physiologic levels in ESR1-knockout MCF7 cells and measuring transcriptional output, receptor half-life, and growth inhibition across a concentration range for fulvestrant, elacestrant, camizestrant, imlunestrant, and giredestrant. Aim 3 will test in NCT03466099 whether switching endocrine partner at the time of a confirmed rise in mutant allele fraction, rather than at radiographic progression, prolongs the interval to clinical deterioration, with 240 patients randomized 1:1 and a primary endpoint of second progression-free survival.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Endocrine resistance driven by ESR1 mutation is a paradigm of acquired, drug-selected genetic change in a solid tumor. The mutations are rare in untreated primary disease, accumulate in proportion to aromatase inhibitor exposure, and predict inferior outcome when treatment is continued unchanged. Several oral antiestrogens designed to retain activity against mutant receptor have entered late-phase testing, yet the field still selects patients using tissue obtained years earlier or using plasma drawn only at progression. Because mutant allele fractions fluctuate by more than an order of magnitude within a single treatment course, a single time point is a poor guide. Establishing the kinetics, the substitution-specific pharmacology, and the value of acting early on plasma change would convert an established observation into a management strategy.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: This proposal treats the plasma mutation profile as a longitudinal signal rather than a static label. Sampling every 4 weeks in 500 patients yields the densest ESR1 time series assembled to date and permits estimation of doubling times for individual substitutions, which we have shown differ by a factor of three in pilot data. The pharmacologic aim uses receptor knock-in at endogenous locus and endogenous expression level rather than overexpression, avoiding the artifact that has made cross-study comparison of mutant sensitivity unreliable. Finally, the embedded randomized trial tests an action, not an association: it asks whether earlier switching helps, which no observational analysis can answer. Together these features move the field from cataloguing mutations toward using their trajectory to time therapy.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Plasma is processed within 4 hours into two 4-mL cell-free DNA aliquots. Droplet digital PCR assays for Y537S, Y537N, Y537C, D538G, E380Q, L536P, L536H, and S463P are run in duplicate with a limit of detection of 0.05 percent. Hybrid-capture sequencing of a 61-gene panel is performed at every third time point. Receptor variants are introduced into MCF7 by CRISPR knock-in and validated by allele-specific sequencing. Transcriptional output is measured by RNA sequencing and by a GREB1 and TFF1 reporter. For the trial, 240 patients provide 85 percent power to detect an improvement in second progression-free survival from 6.5 to 10.0 months at a two-sided alpha of 0.05, assuming 20 percent of participants trigger an early switch and a 12 percent dropout rate.

title: Cyclin E1-CDK2 Signaling as a Therapeutic Vulnerability in CDK4/6 Inhibitor-Refractory Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Resistance to CDK4/6 inhibition frequently proceeds through kinase activity that bypasses the drug target entirely. Cyclin E1, encoded by CCNE1, partners with CDK2 to phosphorylate RB1 at sites that palbociclib cannot protect, allowing passage through the restriction point despite full CDK4 and CDK6 occupancy. CCNE1 amplification or transcript elevation is present in 15 to 22 percent of tumors progressing on palbociclib and predicts short duration of benefit when measured before treatment. Selective CDK2 inhibitors have now reached the clinic, but there is no validated way to identify the tumors that depend on this axis, and no preclinical evidence defining the correct sequence or combination. This project will map cyclin E1 dependency across a panel of patient-derived xenografts and organoids, define an expression threshold that separates responders from non-responders, and test CDK2 inhibition alone and with continued CDK4/6 blockade.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1 will measure cyclin E1 protein, including the low-molecular-weight isoforms generated by elastase cleavage, and CCNE1 transcript across 34 hormone receptor-positive patient-derived xenografts and 18 organoid lines, and correlate these with palbociclib growth inhibition. Aim 2 will determine whether CDK2 inhibition restores control of the G1 to S transition in cyclin E1-high models, using PF-07104091 and BLU-222, with readouts of RB1 phosphorylation at serine 780 and serine 807, E2F target transcript abundance, and DNA replication licensing measured by MCM2 chromatin loading. Aim 3 will test sequential versus concurrent CDK2 and CDK4/6 inhibition in eight xenografts derived from patients who progressed on palbociclib, with tumor growth delay as the primary readout and marrow reserve monitored as the principal dose-limiting concern.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: The clinical failure of CDK4/6 inhibition is not a single phenomenon. Loss of RB1 removes the drug target's substrate and predicts failure of any agent acting upstream, whereas cyclin E1-CDK2 activation leaves RB1 intact and therefore remains addressable. Distinguishing these situations matters because the therapeutic implications are opposite: the first argues for abandoning the pathway, the second for intensifying it. Because CCNE1 amplification and cyclin E1 overexpression are far more common than RB1 loss, the addressable group is the larger one. Establishing a quantitative threshold for cyclin E1 dependency, rather than a categorical amplification call, would allow the first rational assignment of patients to CDK2 inhibitors as these agents move from phase 1 into randomized testing.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Most published work has used CCNE1 copy number as a surrogate for cyclin E1 activity. We show in pilot data that copy number explains only 41 percent of the variance in cyclin E1 protein and almost none of the variance in the low-molecular-weight isoforms, which lack the p21 and p27 binding surface and are therefore refractory to endogenous inhibition. Our proposal measures the isoform-resolved protein directly by capillary immunoassay and pairs it with a functional readout of RB1 phosphorylation site occupancy. We also model the sequencing question explicitly rather than assuming that combination is superior; our pilot suggests that concurrent exposure causes disproportionate marrow suppression while sequential exposure preserves efficacy.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Xenografts are propagated in NSG mice at passage 3 to 6 and authenticated by short tandem repeat profiling. Palbociclib is dosed at 90 mg/kg daily by oral gavage; PF-07104091 at 30 mg/kg twice daily. Cyclin E1 isoforms are resolved on a Simple Western system with recombinant standards. RB1 phosphosite occupancy is quantified by parallel reaction monitoring mass spectrometry. E2F output is summarized as an eleven-transcript score. For Aim 3, eight models with ten mice per arm across four arms give 80 percent power to detect a 40 percent difference in tumor growth delay assuming a coefficient of variation of 0.35. All comparisons use mixed-effects models with model identity as a random effect to avoid pseudoreplication.

title: HER2-Low Biology and Determinants of Antibody-Drug Conjugate Payload Delivery in Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Roughly half of all breast cancers classified as HER2-negative express HER2 protein at immunohistochemistry scores of 1+ or 2+ without gene amplification. This HER2-low population was long treated as biologically uninformative because trastuzumab and pertuzumab provide no benefit there. Trastuzumab deruxtecan changed that: an antibody-drug conjugate with a high drug-to-antibody ratio and a membrane-permeable topoisomerase I payload can produce durable responses at antigen densities far below the threshold for classical HER2-directed therapy. Why some HER2-low tumors respond and others do not is unknown. This U01 will quantify HER2 protein by mass spectrometry and immunofluorescence across 900 tumors, define the antigen density and internalization kinetics required for payload delivery in preclinical models, and dissect the bystander effect that allows killing of antigen-negative neighbors.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1 will establish an absolute HER2 protein scale using selected reaction monitoring mass spectrometry on 900 archival tumors, calibrated against quantitative immunofluorescence, and will determine where in that continuous scale response to trastuzumab deruxtecan begins. Aim 2 will measure receptor internalization and lysosomal trafficking rates in 22 preclinical models spanning two orders of magnitude of HER2 density, using pH-sensitive antibody labeling and live-cell imaging, and will relate these rates to intratumoral deruxtecan concentration measured by imaging mass spectrometry. Aim 3 will quantify the bystander effect by constructing defined mixtures of HER2-low and HER2-null cells and measuring killing of the null population as a function of mixing ratio, spatial arrangement in three-dimensional culture, and payload efflux through ABCC2 and ABCG2.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Immunohistochemistry was designed to identify amplified tumors and was never validated for discrimination within the low range. Concordance between pathologists for the distinction between a score of 0 and 1+ is only moderate, and this distinction now determines access to an effective drug. An absolute protein scale would replace an ordinal assay used outside its design range. Beyond assay reform, the biology matters: if response depends on internalization rate rather than surface density, then tumors with identical staining could differ predictably in benefit, and agents that increase receptor turnover could extend the eligible population. The bystander effect is equally consequential because it determines whether antigen heterogeneity within a tumor limits or is overcome by conjugate therapy.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: We replace an ordinal stain with a calibrated protein measurement expressed in receptors per cell, a scale on which response thresholds can be estimated rather than assumed. We measure trafficking rather than inferring it, using ratiometric pH-sensitive conjugates that report the fraction of bound antibody that has reached the acidic lysosomal compartment within 90 minutes. We measure payload where it acts, by imaging mass spectrometry of tumor sections at 20-micron resolution, rather than in whole-tumor homogenate where stromal dilution obscures gradients. Finally, our defined-mixture platform makes the bystander effect a measured quantity with a diffusion length, which can then be compared across conjugates carrying cleavable and non-cleavable linkers.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Archival blocks come from three institutional cohorts with linked treatment and outcome data. Selected reaction monitoring uses two proteotypic HER2 peptides with heavy-labeled internal standards, with a lower limit of quantification of 30 amol per microgram of protein. Immunofluorescence uses the 4B5 antibody with tyramide amplification and cell-line calibrators of known receptor number. Response thresholds are estimated by fitting a two-component mixture model to the continuous protein measurement against best percentage change in tumor diameter. Imaging mass spectrometry is performed on 12-micron cryosections with a matrix-assisted laser desorption source. Power calculations indicate that 900 tumors, with an anticipated 210 conjugate-treated cases, permit estimation of a response threshold with a 95 percent confidence interval width of approximately 0.4 log units.

title: Overcoming PI3K Pathway-Mediated Resistance After CDK4/6 Inhibition in ER-Positive Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Activating PIK3CA mutations are present in about 40 percent of hormone receptor-positive breast cancers and are enriched further in tumors that have progressed on CDK4/6 inhibitors. Alpelisib with fulvestrant improves progression-free survival in this population, but median benefit is short, roughly 11 months in the registration trial and closer to 7 months after CDK4/6 exposure, and hyperglycemia and rash force dose reduction or interruption in a third of patients. The pathway is therefore validated but poorly exploited. This project asks why the PI3K pathway becomes dominant after CDK4/6 blockade, whether AKT-directed rather than alpha-isoform-directed inhibition is better suited to that setting, and how the metabolic consequences of alpha-isoform inhibition can be blunted so that effective exposure is sustained.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1 will define how PI3K pathway output changes during CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy, using reverse-phase protein arrays and phosphoproteomics on 60 paired biopsies to quantify AKT serine 473, PRAS40, S6 ribosomal protein, and 4E-BP1 phosphorylation before treatment and at progression. Aim 2 will compare alpelisib, capivasertib, and everolimus in ten patient-derived xenografts stratified by PIK3CA and AKT1 genotype, each combined with fulvestrant, with tumor growth delay and duration of control as endpoints. Aim 3 will test whether a ketogenic diet or an SGLT2 inhibitor prevents the insulin feedback that limits alpha-isoform inhibition, measuring glucose, insulin, and tumor phospho-AKT in tumor-bearing mice and in a 40-patient pilot embedded in NCT04073680.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Endocrine resistance after CDK4/6 inhibition is now the commonest clinical scenario in hormone receptor-positive metastatic disease, and PI3K pathway activation is its commonest tractable driver. Yet alpha-isoform inhibition is self-limiting: blocking p110-alpha in muscle and liver raises blood glucose, the resulting insulin surge reactivates the pathway in tumor, and dose interruption for hyperglycemia occurs in 20 to 30 percent of treated patients. This is a pharmacologic problem with a metabolic solution, and preclinical work suggests that suppressing the insulin response restores drug effect. Establishing which patients should receive alpha-isoform versus AKT-directed inhibition, and how to keep them on treatment, would extend a benefit that currently lasts months.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Rather than treating hyperglycemia as a nuisance to be managed after the fact, we treat it as a mechanism of drug failure to be prevented in advance, and we measure the tumor consequence directly through phospho-AKT in serial biopsies rather than inferring it from glucose alone. We also compare three pathway agents head to head in the post-CDK4/6 setting, a comparison that has never been made because each was developed against a different control. Our paired-biopsy design captures the pathway state at the moment of clinical decision-making rather than at diagnosis, which is when the pathway state is currently measured and when it is least informative.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Paired biopsies come from an existing registry with 71 percent progression-biopsy capture. Phosphoproteomics uses tandem mass tag labeling with titanium dioxide enrichment, quantifying approximately 9,000 phosphosites per sample. Xenografts are treated for 60 days or until tumors reach 1,500 cubic millimeters. Mice receive alpelisib 35 mg/kg daily, capivasertib 100 mg/kg on a four-days-on schedule, or everolimus 5 mg/kg daily. The dietary aim uses a 4:1 ketogenic formulation and dapagliflozin at 1 mg/kg. In the clinical pilot, 40 patients provide 80 percent power to detect a reduction in the proportion requiring dose interruption for hyperglycemia from 30 percent to 8 percent using an exact binomial test at one-sided alpha of 0.10.

title: Therapy-Induced Senescence as a Determinant of CDK4/6 Inhibitor Durability

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Palbociclib, ribociclib, and abemaciclib are cytostatic in most hormone receptor-positive breast cancer cells: they impose a durable arrest rather than killing. A large fraction of arrested cells acquire the flattened morphology, beta-galactosidase activity, lysosomal expansion, and inflammatory secretory phenotype of senescence. Senescent tumor cells are not inert. They persist for months, they secrete interleukin 6 and CXCL8, and a fraction of them re-enter proliferation when drug is withdrawn, seeding regrowth. We propose that the durability of CDK4/6 inhibition is set by the balance between how many cells enter this state, how long they remain in it, and how efficiently they are cleared by immune surveillance. This project will quantify that balance and test whether pharmacologic clearance of senescent cells converts a cytostatic response into a lasting one.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1 will quantify the senescent fraction and its persistence during continuous palbociclib exposure in twelve patient-derived xenografts and six organoid lines, using a lysosomal beta-galactosidase reporter, p16 and p21 immunostaining, and an eighteen-gene secretory signature. Aim 2 will define the survival dependencies of the senescent population by CRISPR screening in arrested cells, with validation of BCL-xL, BCL-2, and MCL1 dependence using navitoclax, venetoclax, and A-1331852. Aim 3 will test whether intermittent senolytic exposure after 21 days of palbociclib prolongs the interval to tumor regrowth relative to continuous palbociclib alone, and will determine whether natural killer cell depletion abolishes any benefit, thereby distinguishing direct clearance from immune-mediated clearance.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: The clinical behavior of CDK4/6 inhibitors is unusual: responses are shallow but prolonged, and disease often regrows quickly once the drug is stopped. Both observations are consistent with a large persistent arrested population rather than with tumor cell elimination. If that population is the reservoir from which the disease returns, then eliminating it is a distinct therapeutic goal from deepening the initial arrest, and it requires different drugs. Senolytic agents are already in human testing for age-related indications, so the translational path is short. Establishing that the arrested reservoir governs durability would reframe combination strategy away from adding a second antiproliferative agent and toward clearing cells that have already stopped dividing.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Existing work infers senescence from staining at a single time point in cell lines. We follow the state longitudinally in vivo using a knock-in beta-galactosidase reporter that permits serial intravital imaging of the same tumor, so that entry, persistence, and escape can be measured as rates rather than snapshots. Our CRISPR screen is performed in cells that have already been arrested for 14 days, which is essential because the survival dependencies of arrested cells differ substantially from those of cycling cells. Finally, we test the immune contribution by depletion rather than by correlation, which distinguishes a drug acting on the tumor cell from a drug acting by exposing it to natural killer cells.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Xenografts are established in NSG mice and, for immune experiments, matched syngeneic lines are used in immunocompetent BALB/c hosts. Palbociclib is given at 90 mg/kg daily. Navitoclax is administered at 50 mg/kg on a two-days-per-week intermittent schedule beginning at day 21. The secretory signature is measured by NanoString on laser-captured tumor regions. CRISPR screening uses a 4,000-guide library targeting apoptotic regulators at 500-fold representation. Regrowth is defined as the time from treatment start to a doubling of the nadir tumor volume. Twelve models with eight mice per arm provide 85 percent power to detect a 45 percent extension in time to regrowth, analyzed by mixed-effects Cox regression with model as a random effect.

title: Circulating Tumor DNA-Guided Adaptive Endocrine Therapy and Molecular Residual Disease

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Hormone receptor-positive breast cancer relapses late; half of all distant recurrences occur more than five years after surgery, and current tools cannot identify which women carry residual disease during that interval. In the metastatic setting the same technology problem appears in a different form: treatment is changed only when imaging changes, months after the tumor has already escaped. This U01 applies tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA assays to both settings. We will determine the sensitivity and lead time of molecular residual disease detection after adjuvant endocrine therapy in 1,100 women, characterize the emergence of ESR1 ligand-binding domain mutations and other escape lesions in plasma, and conduct a randomized trial, NCT04567420, testing whether escalating therapy at molecular relapse rather than at radiographic relapse improves distant relapse-free survival.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1 will establish analytic and clinical performance of a personalized 48-variant assay for molecular residual disease in 1,100 women completing surgery and adjuvant endocrine therapy, sampled every 6 months for 6 years, with sensitivity, specificity, and lead time relative to imaging as endpoints. Aim 2 will characterize the plasma genomic profile at molecular relapse, focusing on ESR1 ligand-binding domain substitutions, PIK3CA mutations, and RB1 loss, and will determine which of these are detectable before any radiographic abnormality. Aim 3 will randomize 620 women with detectable molecular residual disease to continued standard adjuvant endocrine therapy or to escalation with fulvestrant plus ribociclib, with distant relapse-free survival as the primary endpoint and a planned interim analysis after 90 events.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Adjuvant endocrine therapy is given to nearly every woman with hormone receptor-positive disease, most of whom are already cured and none of whom can be identified. Extended therapy to ten years yields an absolute benefit of about 3 percent while imposing years of symptoms on the other 97 percent. A test that identifies residual disease would allow escalation for the few and de-escalation for the many. In advanced disease, waiting for imaging change means that a switch of therapy is always made against a larger, more heterogeneous tumor burden than necessary. The value of acting earlier is plausible but unproven, and the only way to establish it is a randomized comparison rather than another observational lead-time study.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Most residual disease studies sample once or twice and report a hazard ratio. We sample every 6 months for 6 years, which permits estimation of the interval between first detection and clinical relapse for each individual and turns a prognostic association into an actionable window. Our assay is personalized to each tumor and tracks 48 variants rather than a fixed gene panel, giving detection at 0.008 percent variant allele fraction, roughly an order of magnitude better than off-the-shelf panels. The randomized escalation aim is designed so that the control arm receives the current standard, meaning that a positive result changes practice immediately rather than requiring a further confirmatory trial.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Whole-exome sequencing of the primary tumor identifies 48 patient-specific somatic variants, which are then tracked in 20 mL of plasma by multiplex PCR followed by deep sequencing at 100,000-fold read depth per amplicon. Detection requires two or more variants above background with a Monte Carlo p value below 0.001. Lead time is estimated by interval-censored survival methods. For the randomized aim, 620 participants with an expected 3-year distant relapse-free survival of 62 percent in the control arm provide 84 percent power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.65 at a two-sided alpha of 0.05, with stratification by nodal status, prior chemotherapy, and time since surgery.

title: Immune Consequences of CDK4/6 Blockade in Estrogen Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: CDK4 and CDK6 are not restricted to tumor cells. Their inhibition alters antigen presentation, derepresses endogenous retroviral transcripts, suppresses regulatory T cell proliferation more than that of effector T cells, and induces a durable arrest accompanied by an inflammatory secretory program that recruits myeloid and lymphoid populations into the tumor bed. These observations suggest that a drug developed as an antiproliferative agent is also an immune modulator, and that combining it with checkpoint blockade could produce responses in a disease where single-agent PD-1 antibodies achieve response rates below 10 percent. This project will define the immune reprogramming caused by abemaciclib in estrogen receptor-positive mammary tumors, determine which effects are tumor-intrinsic and which are host-derived, and identify the schedule that maximizes combination benefit.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1 will characterize the immune landscape after 7, 21, and 42 days of abemaciclib in three estrogen receptor-positive syngeneic mammary models using 42-parameter mass cytometry and indexed droplet transcriptomic profiling of sorted CD45-positive populations. Aim 2 will separate tumor-intrinsic from host-intrinsic effects using CDK6 kinase-dead knock-in tumors in wild-type hosts and wild-type tumors in Cdk6 kinase-dead hosts, with readouts of MHC class I surface abundance, ERV-derived double-stranded RNA, and type III interferon transcription. Aim 3 will compare concurrent, sequential, and intermittent abemaciclib plus anti-PD-1 schedules, with complete regression rate as the primary endpoint and CD8 depletion used to establish dependence on cytotoxic lymphocytes.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Hormone receptor-positive breast cancer is immunologically cold, with low mutational burden and sparse lymphocytic infiltrate, and it has been largely excluded from the benefits of checkpoint blockade. Any intervention that converts this phenotype would apply to the majority of breast cancer patients. CDK4/6 inhibitors are already given to hundreds of thousands of women, so a schedule change rather than a new agent could deliver the effect. However, the same drugs cause neutropenia and lymphopenia, and continuous dosing may suppress the very effector populations that checkpoint blockade requires. Whether the immune benefit and the hematologic penalty can be separated by schedule is the central unanswered question, and it cannot be resolved in immunodeficient systems.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: The kinase-dead knock-in reciprocal chimera design is the key methodologic advance: it allows the drug target to be disabled genetically in either compartment while leaving the other intact, which no pharmacologic experiment can achieve. Second, we profile at three time points spanning the transition from initial arrest to established persistence, capturing the inflammatory secretory program at the moment it appears rather than after it has remodeled the microenvironment. Third, we treat schedule as an experimental variable with three prespecified arms rather than defaulting to continuous concurrent dosing, which our pilot data suggest is the worst of the three because it maintains lymphopenia during the period when effector expansion is required.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Syngeneic models include a Trp53-null estrogen receptor-positive line, an MMTV-driven line propagated with estrogen supplementation, and an organoid-derived transplantable line. Abemaciclib is dosed at 50 mg/kg daily or on a five-days-on two-days-off schedule. Anti-PD-1 clone RMP1-14 is given at 200 micrograms every 3 days. Mass cytometry panels are barcoded to permit 20 samples per acquisition. Double-stranded RNA is quantified by J2 antibody dot blot and by strand-specific sequencing of repeat elements. With ten mice per arm across nine arms we have 82 percent power to detect an increase in complete regression rate from 10 percent to 45 percent by Fisher exact test at a two-sided alpha of 0.05.

title: Adjuvant Abemaciclib and Eradication of Micrometastatic Residual Disease in High-Risk Hormone Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Two years of adjuvant abemaciclib added to endocrine therapy reduces invasive recurrence in women with node-positive, high-risk hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer, with an absolute benefit of roughly 6 percentage points at five years. Three questions follow. Which patients account for that benefit, given that most would never have recurred? Does the benefit persist after the drug is stopped, or is it deferral rather than eradication? And can the substantial early discontinuation seen in the registration trial, where 17 percent of participants stopped abemaciclib prematurely because of diarrhea, be reduced without diluting efficacy? This cooperative group project addresses all three through a randomized phase 3 trial, NCT05138640, with an embedded circulating tumor DNA program and a prophylactic supportive care intervention.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1 will randomize 2,400 women with node-positive disease to two years or four years of adjuvant abemaciclib with standard endocrine therapy, with invasive disease-free survival as the primary endpoint, to determine whether extending exposure converts deferral into cure. Aim 2 will collect plasma at baseline, 6, 12, 24, 36, and 60 months for tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA testing, and will determine whether clearance of detectable disease during the first year identifies the group whose recurrence is prevented. Aim 3 will randomize participants a second time to prophylactic loperamide plus dietary counseling or to reactive management, with the proportion completing 24 months of abemaciclib at the intended dose intensity as the primary endpoint.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Adjuvant intensification decisions in this disease are made almost blind. Genomic assays estimate the risk of recurrence but say nothing about whether a specific added drug will prevent it, and no assay measures whether micrometastatic disease is still present after treatment. Abemaciclib is expensive, is given for two years, and causes diarrhea in the majority of recipients, so the proportion who stop early is large and the cost per recurrence prevented is high. Identifying the group in whom the drug actually eliminates residual disease, rather than delaying its appearance, would allow the other patients to be spared. Extending the treatment duration is the natural test of whether the benefit is durable.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: This is the first adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitor trial designed to test duration rather than to test the drug, and the first to embed serial plasma testing as a prespecified mechanistic endpoint rather than an exploratory correlative. The second randomization to prophylactic supportive care is embedded in the same population, which avoids the usual situation in which supportive strategies are tested in separate small studies whose results cannot be linked to efficacy. Because the trial runs through a cooperative group network of 380 sites, the population will include the community setting where premature stopping is most common and where the registration trial had least representation.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Eligibility requires four or more positive nodes, or one to three nodes with grade 3 histology or tumor size of 5 cm or greater. Randomization is stratified by nodal burden, prior chemotherapy, and menopausal status. Plasma testing uses a personalized 32-variant multiplex assay with a limit of detection near 0.01 percent. With 2,400 participants and 340 expected invasive disease-free survival events we have 85 percent power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.72 at a two-sided alpha of 0.05. For the supportive care randomization, 2,400 participants provide over 90 percent power to detect an increase from 78 percent to 87 percent in the proportion completing the intended 24 months at full dose intensity.

title: Central Nervous System Dissemination in Hormone Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer: Drug Penetration and Tumor Biology

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Brain metastases develop in 10 to 15 percent of women with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer, and their incidence is rising as systemic control improves. Most approved agents for this subtype are substrates of P-glycoprotein and breast cancer resistance protein and achieve unbound concentrations in cerebrospinal fluid that are a small fraction of those in plasma. Abemaciclib is a notable exception, with unbound cerebrospinal fluid concentrations approaching those of plasma, and trastuzumab deruxtecan has produced intracranial responses despite its size. This project will measure unbound drug concentrations in cerebrospinal fluid and in resected central nervous system lesions, define the transporter and microenvironmental determinants of penetration, and characterize how the biology of intracranial lesions differs from that of matched extracranial disease.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1 will measure unbound concentrations of palbociclib, ribociclib, abemaciclib and its M2 and M20 metabolites, alpelisib, and deruxtecan in paired cerebrospinal fluid, plasma, and resected brain lesions from 70 patients undergoing craniotomy or ventricular access, using equilibrium dialysis and liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry. Aim 2 will define transporter dependence using ABCB1 and ABCG2 knockout mice bearing orthotopic intracranial tumors, and will test whether elacridar co-administration raises intracranial exposure sufficiently to change tumor growth. Aim 3 will compare paired intracranial and extracranial lesions from 45 patients by exome and transcriptome sequencing, testing the hypothesis that central nervous system lesions are enriched for RB1 loss, CCNE1 gain, and a distinct astrocyte-adapted metabolic program.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Central nervous system progression in this population is usually treated as a radiotherapy problem because systemic agents are assumed not to reach the site. That assumption is rarely tested with unbound concentrations in the relevant compartment, and where it has been tested the answer differs sharply between agents that appear pharmacologically similar. Getting this right determines whether a woman with limited brain-only progression should receive whole-brain radiotherapy with its cognitive cost, or a change of systemic agent. Beyond drug delivery, if intracranial lesions carry distinct alterations, then treating them by extrapolation from an extracranial biopsy will systematically mis-assign therapy for the compartment that most limits survival.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: We measure the unbound fraction rather than total concentration, which is the only quantity that predicts target engagement and which is almost never reported for central nervous system compartments in breast cancer. We obtain matched cerebrospinal fluid, plasma, and tumor tissue from the same patient at the same moment, permitting calculation of a true tissue-to-plasma partition rather than a surrogate. The transporter aim uses genetic knockout combined with orthotopic intracranial implantation rather than subcutaneous flank tumors, so the blood-tumor barrier is the physiologically relevant one. Finally, cerebrospinal fluid circulating tumor DNA is collected at the same visits, allowing lesion genotype to be tracked without repeat craniotomy.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Patients undergoing clinically indicated craniotomy receive a timed dose 4 to 8 hours before surgery, with plasma and cerebrospinal fluid drawn at incision. Unbound fractions are determined by rapid equilibrium dialysis at 37 degrees. Orthotopic tumors are established by stereotactic injection of 200,000 cells into the right striatum and monitored by bioluminescence. Elacridar is dosed at 100 mg/kg twice daily. Sequencing of paired lesions uses 250-fold exome coverage with matched leukocyte reference. With 70 patients we can estimate a partition coefficient with a coefficient of variation below 25 percent for each agent, and 45 paired lesion sets provide 80 percent power to detect a difference in the prevalence of RB1 loss from 6 percent to 24 percent.

title: A Single-Cell and Spatial Atlas of Endocrine-Resistant Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Bulk sequencing of tumors that have progressed on endocrine therapy and CDK4/6 inhibitors reports the average of a mixture, and the alterations it recovers explain fewer than half of clinical failures. We propose that much of the missing explanation is not genetic but is carried by transcriptional states occupied by a minority of cells and by the spatial organization of the tumor and its stroma. This center project will construct an atlas of endocrine resistance from 160 paired biopsies taken before treatment and at progression, combining single-cell RNA sequencing, single-nucleus ATAC sequencing, and imaging-based spatial transcriptomics. We will define the states that expand under treatment, relate them to clonal evolution inferred from copy number, and map their spatial relationship to fibroblasts and to cytotoxic T cells.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1 will generate paired single-cell transcriptomes from 160 biopsies, targeting 250,000 malignant cells, and will identify transcriptional states whose abundance changes systematically between baseline and progression. Aim 2 will determine whether these states are heritable or plastic by inferring copy-number-defined clonal structure from the same cells and asking whether state occupancy tracks clonal identity or crosses clonal boundaries. Aim 3 will map the states in situ using 960-plex imaging-based spatial transcriptomics on 80 sections, quantifying the distance from each malignant state to CD8-positive T cells, to FAP-positive fibroblasts, and to vasculature, and testing whether resistance-associated states occupy immune-excluded niches enriched for fibroblast-derived FGF and IGF ligands.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Resistance to CDK4/6 inhibition and to endocrine therapy is currently explained genetically in only 40 to 50 percent of cases, and the remaining patients receive treatment chosen without any mechanistic basis. If a substantial share of failures is driven by reversible transcriptional states rather than by fixed mutations, then the therapeutic strategy changes entirely: the target becomes the pathway maintaining the state, and the timing becomes early, before the state is established. Spatial context matters because an identical transcriptional state may be sustained by a fibroblast-derived ligand in one region and be immunologically constrained in another. An atlas at this resolution provides the reference against which mechanistic and therapeutic hypotheses can be tested.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: The design is paired within patient, which removes the between-patient variance that dominates existing single-cell breast cancer datasets and which has made state-abundance comparisons underpowered. We integrate chromatin accessibility from the same specimens, allowing us to ask whether an expanded state carries a stably remodeled regulatory landscape or a transient transcriptional program. The joint inference of clonal structure and transcriptional state from the same cells is unusual and directly addresses the heritability question that determines whether the state is a target or a symptom. All data, including raw sequence, cell-level annotations, and spatial coordinates, are released quarterly through a public portal under a no-embargo policy.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Biopsies are collected on ice and dissociated within 30 minutes using a cold-active protease protocol that preserves fragile luminal epithelium. Single-cell libraries are prepared to a target of 5,000 cells per sample at 50,000 reads per cell. Chromatin accessibility uses a droplet single-nucleus protocol on cryopreserved nuclei. Copy number is inferred with a hidden Markov model over 10-megabase bins, benchmarked against matched exome data. Spatial data are segmented with a nuclear expansion model and validated against immunofluorescence for a nine-marker subset. State abundance changes are tested with a Dirichlet-multinomial mixed model, which controls the compositional false-positive rate that has affected earlier reports. Power simulations indicate detection of a twofold change in a state comprising 4 percent of cells at 80 percent power.

title: Targeted Degradation of the Estrogen Receptor and Cyclin-Dependent Kinases in Endocrine-Resistant Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Fulvestrant, the only approved selective estrogen receptor degrader, removes 40 to 60 percent of receptor protein at achievable exposures and is limited by poor oral bioavailability. Heterobifunctional degraders recruit an E3 ubiquitin ligase to the target and act catalytically, achieving deeper and more sustained loss of protein. Vepdegestrant, a cereblon-recruiting estrogen receptor degrader, eliminates more than 90 percent of receptor at low nanomolar concentrations, including receptor carrying the Y537S substitution that confers endocrine resistance. This project extends targeted protein degradation from the receptor to the kinases downstream of it. We will optimize CDK4-selective and CDK6-selective degraders, determine whether removing the kinase protein rather than inhibiting its catalytic site produces a deeper and more durable arrest, and define the combination behavior of receptor and kinase degraders.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1 will compare vepdegestrant with fulvestrant across a panel of ESR1 genotypes, including wild type, Y537S, Y537N, D538G, and E380Q, measuring degradation half-maximal concentration, receptor half-life, and suppression of GREB1 and TFF1 transcription in knock-in MCF7 and T47D cells and in six xenografts. Aim 2 will develop and characterize CDK4-selective and CDK6-selective degraders based on cereblon and von Hippel-Lindau ligands, defining selectivity by whole-proteome mass spectrometry across 8,500 quantified proteins. Aim 3 will test receptor plus kinase degrader combinations against palbociclib-containing regimens in eight xenografts derived from patients with prior CDK4/6 inhibitor exposure, with depth and duration of tumor regression as endpoints.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Every approved agent in this disease acts by occupancy: the drug must remain bound to block function, and mutations that reduce affinity restore signaling. Degradation acts by removal, so a single degrader molecule can eliminate many target molecules and the pharmacodynamic effect outlives the plasma exposure. This distinction matters most where occupancy is failing, which is precisely the setting of endocrine resistance. Extending the approach to CDK4 and CDK6 addresses a second limitation: kinase inhibitors leave scaffold functions intact, and both kinases have catalytically independent roles in transcriptional regulation and in the DNA damage response. Removing the protein tests whether those scaffold functions contribute to incomplete responses.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Selective removal of CDK4 without CDK6, or the reverse, is not achievable pharmacologically because the ATP pockets are nearly identical, but it is achievable through degradation because ternary complex formation depends on surfaces distant from the pocket. Our lead compounds show 40-fold selectivity between the two, which allows the first clean test of their separate contributions in a tumor. We also apply degrader chemistry to a target-and-ligase pairing chosen from an arrayed screen of 96 ligase-recruiting ligands rather than from the two ligases used by convention, which broadens the tissue-selectivity options. Proteome-wide selectivity is measured for every compound before biological interpretation, a standard rarely met in this literature.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Degradation is quantified by HiBiT-tagged endogenous alleles read every 15 minutes over 24 hours, with half-maximal degradation concentration and maximum degradation fitted from four-parameter curves. Ternary complex formation is measured by time-resolved fluorescence energy transfer and by surface plasmon resonance. Whole-proteome selectivity uses tandem mass tag labeling with 8,500 proteins quantified at 1 percent false discovery rate. Xenografts derived from patients previously exposed to palbociclib are propagated at passage 3 to 5 in NSG mice, with eight animals per arm. Depth of regression is analyzed as best percentage change from baseline volume and duration as time to a doubling of nadir volume, using mixed-effects models with model identity as a random effect.

title: Integrated Genomic and Transcriptomic Landscape of Endocrine-Resistant Metastatic Hormone Receptor-Positive Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We performed whole-exome and RNA sequencing on 212 metastatic biopsies from patients with hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer who had progressed on at least one line of endocrine therapy, with matched primary tumors available for 96. ESR1 ligand-binding domain mutations were present in 21.2 percent of metastases and in none of the matched primaries, establishing them as acquired under treatment. PIK3CA mutations occurred in 38.2 percent, ERBB2 activating mutations in 4.2 percent, NF1 loss-of-function events in 6.6 percent, and RB1 biallelic inactivation in 4.7 percent. Transcriptional analysis identified a subgroup with elevated E2F and MYC target expression despite intact RB1. Clonal evolution analysis of matched pairs showed that endocrine resistance is usually driven by lesions that expanded from minor populations rather than by lesions present in the dominant primary clone.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Approximately three quarters of breast cancers express the estrogen receptor, and essentially all metastatic disease in this group eventually becomes refractory to estrogen deprivation. The genomic basis of that transition has been studied largely in primary tumors, which are removed before the selective pressure of endocrine therapy has been applied and which therefore cannot show what that pressure selects. Reports from small metastatic series have implicated ESR1 mutation, PI3K/AKT pathway activation, and loss of RB1, but the relative frequency of these events, their clonal relationship to the primary tumor, and their transcriptional consequences have not been assessed together in a single cohort. We assembled a prospectively biopsied metastatic cohort with paired primary tissue in order to distinguish selected alterations from pre-existing ones.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients underwent image-guided core biopsy of a metastatic lesion at the time of clinical progression between 2012 and 2016. Exome libraries were sequenced to 220-fold mean target coverage for tumor and 90-fold for matched peripheral blood leukocyte DNA. Somatic calling used a consensus of three callers with a minimum of five supporting reads and a variant allele fraction of at least 4 percent. Variants also present in matched leukocyte DNA were removed from the somatic set and analyzed separately; pathogenic BRCA2 and PALB2 variants identified in that fraction were present in 6.2 percent of patients. RNA libraries were sequenced to 45 million paired reads. Clonal structure was reconstructed with a Dirichlet process model over copy-number-corrected variant allele fractions, and phylogenies were inferred for the 96 matched pairs.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: ESR1 mutations were confined to aromatase inhibitor-exposed patients and rose in frequency with duration of exposure, from 6.9 percent below 12 months to 34.1 percent above 36 months. Y537S and D538G accounted for 71 percent of ESR1 events. PIK3CA mutations were largely clonal and shared with the matched primary, consistent with an early event. RB1 inactivation was always subclonal in the primary when detectable at all and clonal in the metastasis. Tumors with intact RB1 but high E2F output showed elevated CCNE1 and CDK6 transcript levels and shorter time to subsequent progression, with a median of 4.1 versus 9.8 months and a hazard ratio of 1.94 with a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.31 to 2.87.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Our data separate two classes of alteration in endocrine resistance: those present from the outset, such as PIK3CA mutation, and those selected by therapy, such as ESR1 mutation and RB1 loss. Plasma-based work has shown that ESR1 ligand-binding domain mutations detectable before starting an aromatase inhibitor are associated with markedly shorter progression-free survival on that agent, which is consistent with the exposure-dependent enrichment we observe in aromatase inhibitor-treated metastases. Separately, functional profiling across estrogen receptor-positive cell lines has shown that E2F transcriptional output, rather than RB1 mutation status alone, tracks with insensitivity to CDK4/6 inhibition; our finding of an RB1-intact, E2F-high subgroup with rapid progression suggests that this transcriptional axis identifies a clinically distinct population.

title: ESR1 Ligand-Binding Domain Mutations in Plasma Circulating Tumor DNA Predict Inferior Outcome on Aromatase Inhibitor Therapy

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We measured ESR1 ligand-binding domain mutations in pretreatment plasma from 486 patients with hormone receptor-positive advanced breast cancer starting an aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant. Droplet digital PCR assays covering Y537S, Y537N, Y537C, D538G, E380Q, and L536P detected at least one mutation in 28.6 percent of patients previously exposed to an aromatase inhibitor and in 2.1 percent of endocrine-naive patients. Among patients starting a further aromatase inhibitor, median progression-free survival was 3.9 months for mutation-positive versus 8.4 months for mutation-negative disease, with a hazard ratio of 2.12 and a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.61 to 2.79. No such difference was seen among patients starting fulvestrant. Multiple distinct ligand-binding domain substitutions coexisted in 38 percent of mutation-positive samples, indicating that endocrine resistance arises independently in several tumor populations within the same patient.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Estrogen deprivation by aromatase inhibition selects for receptor variants that no longer require ligand. These substitutions cluster in helix 12 of the ligand-binding domain and stabilize the agonist conformation, producing constitutive transcriptional activity. They are essentially absent from untreated primary tumors, so tissue obtained at diagnosis cannot be used to detect them, and metastatic rebiopsy is often impractical. Circulating tumor DNA offers a route to serial measurement, but its clinical value depends on whether detection changes what should be done. Because fulvestrant binds and destabilizes the mutant receptor while aromatase inhibition acts upstream of it, the two classes of agent might be expected to differ in their vulnerability to these mutations, a prediction that has not been tested prospectively at scale.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Plasma was collected before the first dose of endocrine therapy and processed within 4 hours into 4-mL aliquots. Cell-free DNA was extracted from 4 mL and quantified by fluorometry, with a median yield of 24 nanograms. Each of six droplet digital PCR assays was run in duplicate with 20,000 accepted droplets per well and mutant calls requiring three or more positive droplets and a fractional abundance above 0.05 percent. Assay specificity was established on 60 plasma samples from healthy donors. Progression-free survival was analyzed by Cox regression stratified by line of therapy and adjusted for visceral involvement, prior chemotherapy, and performance status. A prespecified interaction test evaluated whether mutation status modified the effect of aromatase inhibitor versus fulvestrant.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Mutation prevalence rose with cumulative aromatase inhibitor exposure, from 11.4 percent below 18 months to 41.7 percent above 36 months. D538G was the commonest single substitution at 44 percent of positive samples, followed by Y537S at 27 percent. Median fractional abundance was 1.9 percent with a range from 0.06 to 42 percent. The interaction between mutation status and treatment class was significant, with a p value of 0.004. Among mutation-positive patients, fulvestrant gave a median progression-free survival of 5.7 months against 3.9 months for a further aromatase inhibitor. Patients carrying three or more distinct substitutions had the shortest outcome at 2.8 months, and their disease burden as measured by total mutant molecules per milliliter was fourfold higher at baseline.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: These results support measuring ESR1 status in plasma before each change of endocrine therapy rather than relying on archival tissue. Sequencing of paired primary and metastatic tumors has shown that ligand-binding domain mutations are absent from matched primaries and appear only in treatment-exposed metastases, which explains why archival testing is uninformative here. The coexistence of several substitutions in more than a third of positive samples argues against a single dominant escape route and suggests that agents retaining activity against all common variants will be required. Our finding that fulvestrant benefit is preserved in mutation-positive disease provides a rationale for the next-generation oral antiestrogens now entering trials, several of which were designed specifically against helix 12 variants.

title: RB1 Alterations and E2F Transcriptional Output Define Intrinsic Insensitivity to CDK4/6 Inhibition in Breast Cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We profiled 58 estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer lines and 14 patient-derived xenografts for sensitivity to palbociclib and related the results to genotype and transcriptional state. RB1-null models were uniformly insensitive, with half-maximal growth inhibition above 3 micromolar, but RB1 status accounted for only 6 of 21 insensitive models. An eleven-gene E2F output score measured before drug exposure separated sensitive from insensitive models with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.88, outperforming RB1 mutation status, CDKN2A deletion, and cyclin D1 amplification. High E2F output in RB1-intact models was associated with CCNE1 amplification or cyclin E1 protein elevation in 9 of 12 cases, and short hairpin depletion of CCNE1 in those models restored palbociclib sensitivity and restored control of the restriction point.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Palbociclib and its congeners act by preventing CDK4- and CDK6-mediated phosphorylation of RB1, thereby holding E2F transcription factors in an inactive complex and blocking entry into S phase. The obvious corollary is that tumors lacking RB1 cannot respond, and this has been confirmed in several systems. What has been much less clear is whether RB1 status is sufficient to predict response, because in clinical series RB1 loss is present in fewer than 5 percent of tumors while primary insensitivity is far more common. Several groups have proposed that the functional state of the pathway, rather than the mutation status of any single gene, determines the response. Testing this requires a panel large enough to separate transcriptional and genetic explanations.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Cell lines were authenticated by short tandem repeat profiling and screened in ten-point dose response over 6 days with CellTiter-Glo readout, in triplicate on three separate occasions. Xenografts were treated with palbociclib at 90 mg/kg daily by oral gavage for 28 days, with eight mice per arm, and response was defined as a tumor growth inhibition index above 60 percent. RNA sequencing was performed on untreated cells and on untreated xenograft tissue. The E2F output score was computed as the mean z-score of MCM2, MCM6, CCNE2, CDC6, E2F1, RRM2, TYMS, PCNA, CDT1, GINS2, and MYBL2. RB1 phosphorylation at serine 780 and serine 807 was quantified by capillary immunoassay at 0, 6, and 24 hours after drug exposure.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Twenty-one of 58 lines were insensitive. Six carried biallelic RB1 inactivation. Of the remaining fifteen, twelve had E2F output scores in the top quartile, and nine of those twelve had CCNE1 amplification or cyclin E1 protein above the panel median. In sensitive models, palbociclib reduced serine 780 phosphorylation by more than 80 percent within 6 hours, while in cyclin E1-high insensitive models serine 807 phosphorylation persisted at 62 percent of baseline despite complete loss of serine 780 signal, indicating continued phosphorylation by a kinase other than CDK4 or CDK6. CCNE1 knockdown reduced serine 807 phosphorylation and shifted the palbociclib half-maximal inhibitory concentration from 2.8 micromolar to 0.21 micromolar across five models.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Resistance to CDK4/6 inhibition is not a binary consequence of RB1 loss. Our data indicate that a transcriptional readout of pathway activity captures a larger and clinically more relevant population, and that within the RB1-intact insensitive group cyclin E1 is the dominant explanation. This has two implications. First, assays used to select patients should measure pathway output rather than single-gene status. Second, the cyclin E1-high group remains addressable because RB1 protein is present, so agents that block the alternative kinase should restore control. Sequencing of metastatic biopsies has independently described an RB1-intact subgroup with elevated E2F and MYC target expression and rapid progression, which we believe corresponds to the population defined functionally here.

title: Acquired RB1 Loss and CCNE1 Amplification in Serial Circulating Tumor DNA from Patients Progressing on Palbociclib plus Fulvestrant

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We analyzed 1,020 plasma samples collected every 8 weeks from 195 patients receiving palbociclib with fulvestrant for hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, using a 74-gene tumor-informed panel with a limit of detection of 0.1 percent variant allele fraction. Alterations detectable at progression but absent at baseline included RB1 truncating or biallelic events in 5.6 percent of patients, CCNE1 copy gain in 16.4 percent, PIK3CA H1047R or E545K in 11.8 percent, and ESR1 ligand-binding domain substitutions in 33.8 percent. Circulating tumor DNA burden began to rise a median of 9.6 weeks before radiographic progression, with an interquartile range of 5.1 to 16.2 weeks. Clonal evolution modeling showed that acquired RB1 events arose in populations that also carried the dominant baseline truncal alterations, indicating direct descent rather than the outgrowth of an unrelated lineage.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Combination of an aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant with a CDK4/6 inhibitor is now standard first- and second-line therapy in hormone receptor-positive advanced breast cancer, yet resistance to CDK4/6 inhibition is essentially universal. Progression biopsies are obtained in a minority of patients, and the alterations reported from such series may not represent the population. Serial plasma sampling offers an alternative that is both repeatable and unbiased with respect to lesion accessibility, and it adds a temporal dimension that tissue cannot: the interval between the appearance of an alteration and the appearance of a radiographic change. We applied dense plasma sampling to a uniformly treated cohort in order to establish which alterations are selected during treatment and when they first become detectable.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients enrolled on an institutional registry beginning palbociclib 125 mg daily on a three-weeks-on one-week-off schedule with fulvestrant 500 mg. Plasma was drawn at baseline and every 8 weeks until progression. Hybrid-capture libraries were sequenced to 20,000-fold raw and 3,000-fold deduplicated depth with unique molecular identifiers. Copy gain was called using a normalized coverage ratio with a threshold of 1.6 relative to a panel of 96 normal plasma controls. Baseline absence was defined as zero supporting molecules in a sample with at least 8,000 informative molecules at that locus. Clonal reconstruction used cancer cell fraction estimates corrected for tumor content inferred from truncal variants. Lead time was estimated by fitting piecewise-linear splines to log-transformed tumor DNA burden and comparing the fitted change point with the RECIST progression date.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median follow-up was 26 months and 168 patients progressed. Baseline circulating tumor DNA was detectable in 88.2 percent. Eleven patients acquired RB1 events, of whom nine had no detectable RB1 alteration in more than 12,000 informative molecules at baseline. Acquired CCNE1 gain was associated with a shorter time to progression, at 7.1 versus 13.4 months, with a hazard ratio of 1.87 and a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.24 to 2.82. PIK3CA H1047R emerged in 23 patients, of whom 14 had wild-type baseline plasma. Patients in whom tumor DNA burden fell below the limit of detection by week 8 had a median progression-free survival of 21.3 months against 8.9 months for those in whom it did not, with a p value below 0.001.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Our findings extend earlier functional work showing that RB1-null models are uniformly insensitive to palbociclib and that an E2F transcriptional output score identifies a larger RB1-intact insensitive population in which cyclin E1 is elevated. We show that the same two lesions, RB1 inactivation and CCNE1 gain, can be acquired under treatment pressure in patients and can be detected in plasma before imaging changes. The clinical implication is that a plasma test performed at 8-week intervals identifies a substantial fraction of patients months before conventional progression, which creates a window in which a change of therapy could be made against a smaller tumor burden. Whether acting in that window improves outcome requires randomized testing.

title: Cyclin E1-CDK2 Activation Confers Palbociclib Resistance and Is Targetable with a Selective CDK2 Inhibitor in Patient-Derived Models

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Elevated cyclin E1 is the commonest correlate of resistance to CDK4/6 inhibition in RB1-intact breast cancer, but whether it is causal and whether it is druggable have not been established in patient-derived systems. We show that enforced cyclin E1 expression in MCF7 and T47D shifts the palbociclib half-maximal inhibitory concentration by 18-fold and 12-fold respectively, and that low-molecular-weight cyclin E1 isoforms produce a larger shift than full-length protein. The selective CDK2 inhibitor PF-07104091 restored control of the cell cycle in these models and in six patient-derived xenografts with high cyclin E1, producing tumor growth inhibition of 71 percent as a single agent and 89 percent combined with palbociclib. Sequential rather than concurrent dosing preserved efficacy while halving the neutrophil nadir, an outcome that has direct implications for how these agents should be combined in preclinical models and in patients.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Serial plasma sequencing in patients progressing on palbociclib with fulvestrant showed that CCNE1 copy gain emerges during treatment in roughly one in six patients and is associated with a shorter time to progression, while acquired RB1 events occur in fewer than 6 percent. That distribution implies that the cyclin E1 axis is the larger of the two addressable problems, since RB1 loss removes the substrate on which any upstream agent depends whereas cyclin E1 elevation leaves the pathway intact and merely bypasses the drug target. CDK2 is the obligate partner of cyclin E1 and is now the subject of several selective inhibitor programs. Here we test causality and therapeutic tractability across cell lines, organoids, and patient-derived xenografts, including models established from patients with documented clinical progression on palbociclib.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Full-length CCNE1 and the elastase-generated low-molecular-weight isoforms T1 and T2 were expressed from a doxycycline-inducible cassette at levels within twofold of those seen in CCNE1-amplified tumors, verified by capillary immunoassay against recombinant standards. Fourteen patient-derived xenografts were characterized for cyclin E1 protein and CCNE1 copy number. Preclinical models were treated with palbociclib at 90 mg/kg daily, PF-07104091 at 30 mg/kg twice daily, or combinations given concurrently or in 7-day alternating blocks, with eight mice per arm. RB1 phosphosite occupancy was measured by parallel reaction monitoring. DNA replication licensing was assessed by chromatin-bound MCM2. Neutrophil counts were obtained weekly. Growth data were analyzed with mixed-effects models treating xenograft identity as a random effect.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Induction of low-molecular-weight cyclin E1 sustained serine 807 phosphorylation of RB1 at 74 percent of baseline during palbociclib exposure and maintained MCM2 chromatin loading, whereas full-length cyclin E1 sustained it at 48 percent. PF-07104091 reduced serine 807 phosphorylation to 12 percent and produced G1 accumulation in both settings. Across six cyclin E1-high xenografts, single-agent CDK2 inhibition gave 71 percent tumor growth inhibition and the concurrent combination gave 89 percent, but concurrent dosing reduced the neutrophil nadir to 0.6 times ten to the ninth per liter. Alternating 7-day blocks achieved 84 percent inhibition with a nadir of 1.4. In three cyclin E1-low xenografts, CDK2 inhibition produced 19 percent inhibition, confirming dependence on the axis.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: These data establish cyclin E1 as a causal driver rather than a passenger correlate of palbociclib resistance and identify low-molecular-weight isoforms as the more potent form, which matters because standard immunohistochemistry does not resolve them. The efficacy of sequential dosing is the most immediately actionable finding: marrow suppression is the principal barrier to combining two cell cycle-directed agents, and alternating blocks preserved most of the benefit at half the hematologic cost. Functional profiling across estrogen receptor-positive lines previously showed that an E2F output score identifies insensitive models better than RB1 status, and our results suggest that within that group cyclin E1 protein, resolved by isoform, is the assay that should guide assignment to CDK2 inhibition.

title: Serial Circulating Tumor DNA Allele Fractions of ESR1 Mutations Define Early Molecular Progression During Fulvestrant

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We collected plasma every 4 weeks from 224 patients receiving fulvestrant for hormone receptor-positive advanced breast cancer and tracked eight ESR1 ligand-binding domain substitutions by droplet digital PCR, with confirmatory 61-gene sequencing at every third time point. A confirmed twofold or greater rise in mutant allele fraction on two consecutive draws preceded radiographic progression by a median of 11.4 weeks, with an interquartile range of 6.0 to 18.7. Sensitivity for subsequent progression within 6 months was 78 percent and specificity was 84 percent. Clonal dynamics differed by substitution: Y537S rose steadily during treatment and dominated at progression in 61 percent of patients carrying it, whereas D538G allele fractions fell in 44 percent of patients even as total tumor DNA increased, indicating that the two variants are under different selective pressure during fulvestrant exposure.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Treatment decisions in advanced hormone receptor-positive breast cancer are triggered by imaging performed every 8 to 12 weeks, so a change of therapy always follows the underlying escape by an unknown interval. Plasma measurement of tumor DNA could shorten that interval, but only if the signal is specific enough to act on. Earlier work established that ESR1 ligand-binding domain mutations measured in pretreatment plasma predict inferior progression-free survival on a further aromatase inhibitor while fulvestrant benefit is preserved, and that several distinct substitutions frequently coexist in the same patient. Those observations were cross-sectional. Whether the trajectory of individual substitutions during treatment carries additional information, and whether a defined rise can serve as an early trigger, has not been established.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Eligible patients were starting fulvestrant 500 mg with or without a CDK4/6 inhibitor. Plasma was drawn at baseline, day 15, and every 4 weeks thereafter. Droplet digital PCR assays covered Y537S, Y537N, Y537C, D538G, E380Q, L536P, L536H, and S463P, each run in duplicate with 20,000 accepted droplets. Molecular progression was prespecified as two consecutive draws showing at least a twofold increase in mutant allele fraction above the on-treatment nadir, with the second draw at least 4 weeks after the first. Imaging was performed every 8 weeks and read centrally, blinded to plasma results. Lead time was estimated by interval-censored methods. Clonal composition was reconstructed at each time point from copy-number-corrected fractions using the 61-gene panel.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: At least one ESR1 substitution was detected in 96 patients, 42.9 percent of the cohort. Molecular progression was observed in 71 of these, and 64 subsequently progressed radiographically. Seven met the molecular criterion without progressing within 6 months, giving a false-positive proportion of 9.9 percent among mutation-positive patients. Median lead time was 11.4 weeks. Among patients carrying both Y537S and D538G, the Y537S fraction exceeded the D538G fraction at progression in 68 percent of cases, reversing the baseline ordering in 31 percent. Total tumor DNA burden at week 4 was independently associated with progression-free survival with a hazard ratio of 1.62 per log unit and a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.28 to 2.05.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: A defined, confirmed rise in mutant allele fraction identifies escape roughly three months before imaging does, and does so with a false-positive proportion low enough to justify testing an intervention. The divergent behavior of Y537S and D538G is the more biologically interesting result. Y537S stabilizes the agonist conformation most strongly and is the least responsive to fulvestrant in reporter systems, so its progressive dominance during fulvestrant exposure is consistent with direct selection. This has implications for agent choice at the time of molecular progression, since a treatment that is equally weak against the emerging population would waste the lead time that the assay provides. A randomized test of early switching is now underway.
